skill.name: email-sequence-designer
skill.description: Design lifecycle email automation flows with triggers, timing, branch logic, send caps, quiet hours, sunset rules, and SEND N scoring. Use it before writing individual emails or running a final email quality audit.
skill.summary: Designs lifecycle email sequences with cadence rules and SEND N scoring.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline paths, relative documentation links, and GitHub metadata. One medium risk remains: SKILL.md line 52 instructs agents to run a Resend connector that can schedule or send email when rerun with --live. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Live ESP connector execution can mutate email campaigns.
remediation.suggestion: Keep dry-run as the default, require explicit user confirmation before --live, quote all CLI arguments, and verify consent and suppression records before scheduling.

content.value_statement: Email programs often lack clear triggers, timing, exits, and fatigue controls. This skill turns lifecycle goals into structured flow maps with cadence governance and SEND N scoring.
actual_capabilities: Maps welcome, abandoned-cart, browse-abandon, post-purchase, re-engagement, and cold-outbound flows.
Defines triggers, delays, branch logic, exit conditions, and goals for each sequence step.
Sets global send caps, quiet hours, fatigue guardrails, and sunset rules.
Produces a SEND N dimension score with sub-item notes and the active goal-weight column.
Creates handoff summaries for creative writing, consent checks, and final quality auditing.
limitations: Does not write the final subject lines, body copy, or calls to action.
Does not compute the full goal-weighted EQS or enforce final SEND vetoes.
Requires user-provided triggers, segments, or exports for measured recommendations.
Closed-loop lapsed-customer re-permission programs belong to the reactivation specialist skill.

use_cases.title: Launch an onboarding series
use_cases.description: Create a welcome flow with enrollment triggers, step timing, exit rules, and graduation into the next lifecycle stage.

use_cases.title: Recover cart and browse intent
use_cases.description: Plan abandoned-cart and browse-abandon sequences with purchase exits, discount branches, and frequency controls.

use_cases.title: Govern list fatigue
use_cases.description: Define send caps, quiet hours, fatigue throttles, and sunset paths for subscribers with declining engagement.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: welcome flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a welcome flow for [product] and [audience]. Trigger is [signup event]. Include timing, goals, exits, and send caps.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: abandoned cart
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an abandoned-cart sequence for [store]. Use [number] steps, [timing], purchase exits, discount logic, and quiet hours.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: lifecycle audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these current lifecycle flows: [paste summary]. Identify gaps, redesign cadence, add branch logic, and score SEND N.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: multi-flow governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Design welcome, cart, browse, post-purchase, and re-engagement flows for [segments]. Add global send caps, sunset policy, and handoff notes.

output_examples.input: Design a welcome sequence for a new SaaS trial.
output_examples.output: A five-step onboarding flow with signup trigger, activation goals, delay schedule, role-based branches, trial-conversion exits, and SEND N notes.

output_examples.input: Plan an abandoned-cart flow for a clothing store.
output_examples.output: A three-step recovery sequence with cart trigger, purchase exit, discount branch, quiet-hour rules, complaint guardrails, and handoff recommendations.

output_examples.input: Reduce fatigue in an active newsletter list.
output_examples.output: A cadence plan with rolling send caps, engagement-decay throttles, re-engagement touch, sunset threshold, and open loops for missing consent data.

best_practices: Provide the trigger event, target segment, lifecycle goal, and current cadence before asking for a flow map.
Confirm consent, suppression, unsubscribe, and bounce rules before activating any sequence.
Send the completed flow map to creative and audit skills before live deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to write complete email copy for every step.
Do not use it to bypass consent, suppression, unsubscribe, or quiet-hour rules.
Do not treat estimated timing as measured performance data.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces lifecycle flow maps, cadence rules, branch and exit logic, sunset paths, and a SEND N dimension score.

faq.question: Can it write the emails?
faq.answer: No. It designs the sequence structure. Use an email creative skill to write subject lines, body copy, and calls to action.

faq.question: Can it activate sends in an ESP?
faq.answer: It can describe a guarded Resend connector workflow, but live sends require user confirmation and consent checks.

faq.question: Does it handle re-permission win-back programs?
faq.answer: No. Use a reactivation specialist for closed-loop win-back or re-consent programs on lapsed cohorts.

faq.question: What inputs improve results?
faq.answer: Useful inputs include segment definitions, trigger events, ESP exports, unsubscribe data, complaint rates, and conversion goals.

faq.question: Is it useful in Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is Markdown-based and works with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill hosts.
